abstract: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is characterized by oligodendroglial -synuclein inclusions, although neuronal inclusions also occur. We investigated whether regional differences in -synuclein filament structure are associated with distinct cytopathologies in a neuropathologically confirmed MSA brain by comparing the medial temporal lobe, which showed prominent neuronal inclusions and limited oligodendroglial pathology, with cerebellar white matter, which contained exclusively oligodendroglial inclusions. Cryo-electron microscopy resolved filaments from these regions at 3.0 [A] and 2.0 [A], respectively. Medial temporal filaments contained a previously undescribed protofilament fold, PF-IIIA, paired with canonical PF-IIB2, whereas cerebellar filaments adopted the canonical MSA Type II structure. PF-IIIA exhibits extensive remodeling of its core while retaining the asymmetric doublet architecture. These findings reveal regional -synuclein structural heterogeneity within a single MSA brain and suggest a potential association between distinct filament conformations and neuronal versus oligodendroglial cytopathology, highlighting the importance of regional and cellular context in filament organization and disease heterogeneity.
